Thousands of snow geese fall dead from sky in Idaho

I was curious about this statement:

> Avian cholera is believed to be the culprit in the deaths mostly because of the way the birds died, he said.

> “Basically, they just fell out of the sky,” said Losinski.

It's counter-intuitive that a sick animal suddenly falls out of the sky rather than "withering away" on the ground. So I found this on wikipedia:

> an outbreak of acute avian cholera follows. Infected birds will die 6–12 hours after contracting the bacterium

But nothing else in particular is mentioned on what would make them fall out of the sky, something that seems to happen quite often to birds but is usually left unexplained.

Do we have a unidan over here?

Migrating geese spend a lot of time in flight, don't they? If one is going to die suddenly, reasonable chance it'll happen in the air. Meanwhile a bird that has taken shelter will leave a more concealed corpse in a bush or something.

Not an ornithologist.

Yeah… suppose it would be something like that. Just hard to imagine that something fatally ill would be flying at all, let alone migrating. But then again it's not uncommon for sick or wounded animals to pretend that nothing is wrong out of fear of getting picked off by predators.
I don't trust a goose to know how sick it is.
